notes: Source-verified (not documented-knowledge): Chatwoot ships a live 'Captain' AI feature. config/routes.rb:64-104 defines a captain namespace with tasks_controller actions (rewrite/summarize/reply_suggestion/label_suggestion/follow_up), each backed by a real service in lib/captain/*.rb (non-enterprise) that calls RubyLLM/OpenAI-compatible chat.ask(...) (lib/captain/base_task_service.rb:68-83). config/features.yml:240-242 shows captain_tasks is enabled:true with no premium:true gate, i.e. on by default in the OSS/self-hosted edition â€” this is NOT an enterprise-only feature. Auth: app/controllers/api/base_controller.rb:4-6 requires Devise session or api_access_token on every API request; tasks_controller additionally runs Pundit authorize(:'captain/tasks') (app/policies/captain/tasks_policy.rb allows any authenticated account user â€” no anonymous access). FUNCTIONAL CAVEAT: lib/captain/base_task_service.rb:43-44 short-circuits with {error: 'captain.api_key_missing', error_code: 401} if no OpenAI-compatible API key is configured (system-wide InstallationConfig row or per-account 'openai' integration hook) â€” so the endpoint is live/wired/auth-gated but will return a functional-not-configured error rather than a real completion unless an admin has supplied a key. This is why has_ai_surface is 'partial' rather than 'yes': the surface is real and reachable (with auth) but its downstream LLM call is gated on deployment config, not just on auth. Fuller AI-agent features (captain_integration, copilot_threads, faq_suggestions, embeddings) ARE enterprise/premium-gated (config/features.yml:143-146, enabled:false) and code lives under enterprise/ â€” do not conflate with the always-on tasks endpoints above. Frontend AI UI: app/javascript/dashboard/components-next/copilot/ and .../captain/ trees exist and are wired to these endpoints, not cosmetic.
